messages:
maria: heads-up - Acme (enterprise) opened an escalation: p95/p99 latency regressions on routes that use function calling + structured output validation. Started ~2026-03-14 17:40 UTC after a deploy. They see overall inference times fine, but end-to-end API p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms and p99 to ~980ms. They provided traces and a repro curl.

alex: thanks - can you paste the trace IDs and the exact request they used? any sample request_id or org id?

maria: pasted below. request_id: req_0a3f8c, org: acme-enterprise. customer sample curl:

```:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openchat-32k",
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Find the price for product X and return JSON."}],
    "function_call": "auto",
    "structured_output": {
      "schema": {
        "type":"object",
        "properties": {"price":{"type":"number"}, "currency":{"type":"string"}}
      }
    },
    "stream": false
  }'
```

maria: They said stream=false and rely on server-side schema validation + tool router to route to pricing microservice. Logs from our gateway show long "postproc.validation" spans.

acme-cs-bot: attached trace snippets (redacted):

```:
{ "trace_id": "trace_aa11", "spans": [
  {"name":"inference.decode","dur_ms": 95},
  {"name":"postproc.tool_router","dur_ms": 280},
  {"name":"postproc.validation.jsonschema","dur_ms": 210}
]}
```

li: interesting - both tool_router and jsonschema up. model decode is fine. any CPU spikes on the worker nodes? which runtime variant are they hitting?

maria: node labels: redwood-runtime-v2, instance type g4dn. Customer said they didn't change their prompt. Issue started after our deploy last night (rollout id rollout-2026-03-14-21).

alex: quick hypothesis - in v2 we changed structured output validation to run synchronously and we also added a routing pass that requests tool metadata from the tool-router synchronously (to decide which tool to call). That could add two sequential blocking steps. If validation is CPU-heavy (large schemas) or uses Python jsonschema validation on the critical path, it will add 100s of ms.

jen (oncall): can we reproduce locally with a similar schema and payload? I can spin up a small test hitting runtime with stream=false and measured spans. If we reproduce, we can test mitigations (async validation, schema caching, avoiding round-trip to tool-router).

alex: yes - repro steps:
1) call endpoint with stream=false and a 4-field schema and function_call:auto
2) capture spans via X-Request-ID
3) observe postproc spans

example run I did in staging:
```:
# request
POST /v1/chat/completions
body: same as above

# trace
postproc.tool_router: 240ms
postproc.validation.jsonschema: 190ms
```

li: looks consistent. I dug into flamegraphs on runtime nodes - validation uses jsonschema with Draft-7 and we build a validator per request (no caching). Building validators is linear in schema size and expensive in CPython. Also tool-router fetches tool manifest from service on every request (sync call), no local cache.

maria: customer asked for mitigation ASAP - they need a patch or flag; they're on dedicated capacity but want low-latency SLO.

alex: proposed mitigations (short term -> long term):
- short term (fast to deploy): enable schema caching per process keyed by schema hash; short TTL (e.g., 10m). Also make tool-router metadata fetch asynchronous with best-effort cache; if metadata missing, fallback to simple router rule and proceed. This reduces extra RTT.
- immediate emergency toggle: add org-level flag to disable structured_output validation and skip schema checks for that org (risky but acceptable as temporary workaround under their approval).
- medium: stream-aware validation: perform incremental/streaming validation so we can start sending tokens while validating partials (harder).
- long term: move validation to a separate light-weight worker pool (non-blocking for token path) and return early with a validation job id for audit.

jen: agree. For now let's try schema caching + tool manifest caching rollout. I can push a quick patch to staging to enable validator caching (threadlocal LRU) and tool manifest local cache.

maria: customer is willing to test an org-flag. We should ask legal/security before disabling validation entirely. Also they'd accept a temporary per-org bypass where we still log and later validate off-path.

sam (product): we need to capture risk/telemetry. If we add bypass flag, toggle should be visible in Console with clear notes: "skips schema validation for structured output - may reduce correctness guarantees." Also add audit log entry.

alex: created a PR draft: refactor jsonschema usage to use cached compiled validators; added simple in-process LRU (max 1024 entries) + metric: structured_validation.cache_hit_ratio. Also added an env flag REDWOOD_STRUCTURED_VALIDATION_CACHE=true. Patch link: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/482

li: deployed to staging - I ran load test for 10k requests with schema reuse and saw p95 drop from 420ms to 160ms; p99 from 980ms to 240ms. tool_router improvement after local caching of tool manifests gave another ~40ms.

maria: excellent. Can we expose the env flag as an org-level toggle quickly? Customer would prefer not to wait for full deploy.

alex: we can expose a temporary org-level override in the control plane: set org setting structured_output_validation_mode: "legacy"|"disabled"|"cached". I'll coordinate with infra to wire it to runtime via config push.

jen: oncall checklist:
- add a throttling rule if postproc spans > 500ms to avoid cascading backlog
- add extra logging/tracing for validation path
- rollback rollout-2026-03-14-21 as a last resort if mitigation not sufficient

maria: I updated the customer: "we're rolling out a cache for validators and tool manifests to staging now; can push to your dedicated nodes within 2 hours if you want. Alternatively we can enable a temporary bypass flag per-org but that disables server-side schema checks - recommended only with compensating checks on your side." They asked to try the cached option first.

acme-cs-bot: confirmed. Please push to their dedicated pool.

alex: action items:
- alex: finish PR and get canary to staging (ETA 1h)
- li: add tool-manifest local cache and verify TTL behavior (ETA 2h)
- jen: prepare rollback playbook + throttling rule (ETA 30m)
- sam: coordinate with legal/security to allow temporary bypass if needed (ETA 4h)
- maria: keep customer updated and collect a couple of failing trace ids post-push

li: note on implementation: cache keys should include schema hash + validator options (e.g., allow_unknowns). Invalidation TTL 10m + metric to know eviction churn. For tool-manifest, Keyed by tool_id + version header; fallback to simple router heuristics if remote not reachable.

jen: live incident notes: if enabling cache doesn't help, we will escalate to rollback. Keep me posted.

maria: will push to acme dedicated pool in ~90m and share traces.

acme-support: thanks team. We'll monitor and report back.
